title: How Steve Jobs responded to Apple's toxic engineering culture: own the mess, keep the debate
summary: In a 1997 email exchange, Avie Tevanian argues Apple's culture is a recurring "cancer" and floats selling the company. Jobs agrees employees dodge responsibility for bad products, marketing and support, but insists Apple is worth saving as the only alternative to Windows. He also asks Avie to keep challenging him, because disagreement is how the team reaches the right decisions.

principles.text: Bad outcomes have authors; a failing company's people must own shared responsibility for the mess.
principles.quote: They just don’t want to share any responsibility for the current state of the company…

principles.text: Ask who actually made the bad products, marketing and support instead of blaming circumstances.
principles.quote: I don’t know who they think engineered and shipped such bad products, who created and authorized such bad marketing, who caused the support to be so bad, etc…

principles.text: Even in a bad state, a company is worth saving if it fills a unique role no one else does.
principles.quote: But, there is something good here worth saving. I don’t quite know how to express it, but it has to do with the fact that Apple is the ONLY alternative to Windows and that Apple can still inject some new thinking into the equation.

principles.text: Invite challenge from close colleagues; productive disagreement is how teams reach the right decisions.
principles.quote: Please continue to challenge me. It’s the way we get to the right decisions, and I enjoy it too.

principles.text: Work through hard strategic questions in person, not over email.
principles.quote: Let’s go for a walk and talk about this sometime soon,
